title: Local Estimation Framework for the Behavioral Layer: Departure Hazard, Latent Awareness, and Destination Choice
design_markdown:
# Estimation Framework for the Behavioral Layer (Chunk 2)

**Design goal.** Replace the ~15 ASSUMED behavioral coefficients (registry census: every hazard-departure and choice-utility coefficient is class A — `Geography/data/registry/variables.csv:40-48`, rows V35–V43) with locally estimated posteriors that **drop into the existing engine unchanged**. The engine's parameter surface already exposes every target as a named batch parameter (`alphaHazard`, `bRisk`, `wOfficial`, `gammaVuln`, `riskHalfLifeH`, `sigmaTheta`, `barrierBelongings`, `barrierPet`, `barrierDependents`, `lambdaOutreachPerDay`, `betaTravelTime`, `betaCapacityPrior` — `Geography/src/geography/agents/ContextCreator.java:274-294`), so point estimates and posterior draws require **zero code changes**: posterior uncertainty propagates by running the engine at M posterior draws through the existing multi-run sweep/verification infrastructure (the same family pattern as the archived BS/W/E sweeps).

**Ground rule inherited from the repo.** The project's own decision document states that no fitted quantitative choice model for unsheltered people and shelters exists anywhere in the literature, and explicitly warns against inventing separate sub-parameters where evidence supports one latent construct (`docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:84-94`). This framework therefore estimates **exactly the coefficients the engine already has**, adds auxiliary covariates only as specification tests (never as drop-in parameters), and shrinks the three barrier coefficients toward a shared value.

---

## 1. DEPARTURE: discrete-time hazard (person-hour logit)

### 1.1 The implemented predictor (what estimates must map onto)

The engine evaluates departure **once per hour** (`newHour` gate, GisAgent.java:371-374, 403) for every aware, not-yet-departed resident:

```
u_i(t) = alphaHazard
       + bRisk · (1 + gammaVuln · 1{vuln_i}) · z_R(t)
       + wOfficial · 1{open(t)}
       + sigmaTheta · thetaZ_i
       − c_i
p_i(t) = logit⁻¹(u_i(t));   depart iff open(t) AND U < p_i(t)
```
(GisAgent.java:408-414), with

- `z_R(t) = z_R(t−1)·2^(−1/riskHalfLifeH) + 1{C(t) ≥ 55.5}/24` — a decayed integrator of unhealthy-hours, deterministic, updated hourly (GisAgent.java:378-379);
- `vuln_i = copd ∨ asthma ∨ age≥65 ∨ mobilityLimited` (GisAgent.java:405-407);
- `c_i = barrierBelongings·B_i + barrierPet·P_i·1{world refuses pets} + barrierDependents·D_i`, precomputed once (GisAgent.java:939-943);
- `thetaZ_i ~ N(0,1)` iid per person, scaled by `sigmaTheta` (GisAgent.java:938).

### 1.2 Estimation model

**Data unit:** person-hour rows for aware, at-risk individuals i in hours t from event onset until departure/attempt, censoring, or event end. **Outcome:** y_it = 1 if i sets out (or presents at a shelter) in hour t.

**Primary (engine-aligned) linear predictor:**

```
logit h_it = α* + β_R (1 + γ_V v_i) z_R(t; τ½) + θ_i − (κ_B B_i + κ_P P_i π_t + κ_D D_i)
```

where τ½ (the half-life) is a **fitted parameter** inside the z_R construction, π_t is the prevailing pet-refusal environment, and the risk set includes only hours with ≥1 open shelter.

**A hard identifiability fact, from the code as written:** the engine only permits departure when `open(t)` is true (`if (open && decisionRng.nextDouble() < p)`, GisAgent.java:414), so **every realized departure hour has 1{open}=1**. In any data generated by — or consistent with — this mechanism, `wOfficial` is perfectly collinear with `alphaHazard`. The estimable intercept is the sum:

```
α* = alphaHazard + wOfficial
```

Consequences: (a) estimate α*; (b) `wOfficial` separately requires either stated-intent survey items ("would you have gone before a shelter officially opened?") or a design contrast across events with/without official announcement — it is **not identifiable from arrival/occupancy data at all**; (c) for drop-in, fix `wOfficial` at a declared scenario value (its registered anchor is the Tanim 2022 pooled OR, per registry row V37, variables.csv:42 — content per audit inventory) and set `alphaHazard = α̂* − wOfficial`. The current default −8.0 is explicitly provisional pending the E9 refit (ContextCreator.java:279-282), and E9 has never been run (no E9 archive exists in docs/runs — ABSENT, per audit inventory).

**Covariates requested vs. engine slots — the drop-in discipline:**

| Requested covariate | Engine slot | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| PM2.5 level C(t), dynamics ΔC(t) | none — only z_R enters u | **Specification-test covariates only.** Because the smoke field is county-uniform (one scalar per hour; audit inventory, SmokeField.java + md:210), C(t), ΔC(t), and z_R(t) are all functionals of a single temporal series: they are severely collinear and purely temporal. Fit the engine-aligned z_R spec as primary; add log C(t) and ΔC(t) in an expanded spec. If they carry load, report a **functional-form finding** (the integrator is wrong), not extra coefficients. |
| Outreach contact (time-varying) | not in u; outreach is the awareness-conversion channel, hourly Bernoulli(λ/24) (GisAgent.java:384-393) | Enters the **awareness sub-model** (§2), not the hazard. Putting outreach into the hazard would estimate a coefficient with no engine slot. |
| Shelter-open indicator | wOfficial·1{open} | Absorbed into α* (collinearity above); defines the risk set. |
| Mobility | only inside vuln_i interaction on the z_R slope (GisAgent.java:405-409) | Estimate γ_V on the composite vulnerable flag exactly as coded. A mobility **main effect** has no engine slot; test it in the expanded spec as a misfit diagnostic. |
| Pets | κ_P inside c_i, active only under a pet-refusing environment (GisAgent.java:941) | Estimate κ_P interacted with policy environment; drop-in via `barrierPet` + `petPolicyDefault` (ContextCreator.java:288, 293). |
| Group membership (dependents) | κ_D inside c_i; also group speed delta V34 (movement, not departure — ELayerSampler.java:75-83) | Estimate κ_D in c_i. |

Per 04-DECISION.md:91-94, place a **hierarchical shrinkage prior pulling κ_B, κ_P, κ_D toward a common κ̄** (the baseline-real arms already use a single 0.26 for all three, per audit inventory, PORT_MAP.md:369-371): `κ_j ~ N(κ̄, σ_κ²)` with a tight prior on σ_κ. Three free unshrunken barrier coefficients from thin data is exactly the failure mode the repo warns against.

### 1.3 Hierarchical structure and partial pooling

```
θ_i = u_{a(i)} + e_i,   u_a ~ N(0, σ_area²),   e_i ~ N(0, σ_person²)
```

- **Origin areas a:** spatial aggregates of campsite locations — never raw coordinates. The encampment file's per-row `inc_date`/location structure supports area construction (audit inventory, data section), and areas must respect the repo's disclosure floor (aggregate ≥5 *reports* per zone, per the project's data-disclosure posture note). Area intercepts also absorb spatial confounding; in particular, if fitted u_a correlate with network distance to the nearest shelter, that is evidence distance belongs in the **departure** model — a mechanism the engine currently does not have — and must be reported as an extension finding, not silently dropped in.
- **Drop-in caveat (honest):** the engine draws thetaZ **iid per person** on a private decision stream (ELayerSampler.java:31-35; GisAgent.java:937-938). Area-level correlation has no engine slot. Two options: (i) marginal-variance mapping, `sigmaTheta ← sqrt(σ_area² + σ_person²)` — preserves each agent's marginal heterogeneity but understates between-area outcome correlation (state this in the manuscript); (ii) a small sampler extension drawing u_a per area then e_i per person — a code change, to be R3-gated (the E0-null byte-identity regression, audit inventory validation section) like every prior layer addition.
- **Frailty identifiability warning:** with single-spell data (one event, one departure per person), σ_person is identified only through the deviation of the aggregate hazard shape from the covariate-implied shape — a functional-form-dependent, weak identification (standard result for univariate frailty in single-spell duration data). Unless repeated-decision data exist (e.g., nightly return/stay decisions across the 9 shelter nights, which linked nightly logs would provide), keep `sigmaTheta` as a **scenario axis with an informative prior**, and report its posterior only with a prior-sensitivity panel.

### 1.4 Likelihood with latent awareness

Awareness is latent (§2). The person-level likelihood marginalizes the two-state chain UNAWARE → AWARE (absorbing), exactly mirroring the engine's states (GisAgent.java:384-393, 953-958):

```
L_i = p₀ · L_i(hazard | aware from t₀)
    + (1−p₀) · Σ_k P(convert at hour k | λ) · L_i(hazard | aware from k)
    + (1−p₀) · P(never convert | λ) · 1{no departure observed}
```

This is a short forward recursion (an HMM with one transition), directly implementable in Stan or PyMC.

---

## 2. AWARENESS: latent binary with an informative local prior

### 2.1 Implemented mechanism

Initial awareness ~ Bernoulli(pAwareInit) drawn at build; the sourced value is 26/73 = 0.356 from the PSU "Stories from the Outside" survey of this event (N=73; 65% did not hear about the shelters; Wilson 95% CI 0.25–0.47) — ELayerSampler.java:39-46 and 04-DECISION.md:44-63. Unaware residents sit in State.UNAWARE, converting only via the hourly outreach Bernoulli(λ/24) (GisAgent.java:384-393); λ is registered UNSOURCED (A-31; "a real outreach-contact rate for this event does not exist in the record" — audit inventory, registry V41).

### 2.2 Prior

Treat the survey as binomial evidence: **p₀ ~ Beta(26.5, 47.5)** (Jeffreys update of 26/73; posterior mean 0.355, matching the engine constant and its Wilson CI). Because the survey is non-probability, BIPOC-oversampled by design, and retrospective by ~9 months (04-DECISION.md:61-63), add a **power-prior discount** δ ∈ {1, 0.5, 0.25} on the survey likelihood and report all three — the discount grid is a declared robustness axis, not a data claim.

### 2.3 How outreach-contact data would update it

The engine's λ is a **compound**: contact rate × per-contact conversion. Operational outreach logs (contacts per person-day, if a provider's records were obtained — currently ABSENT) identify the contact rate; the conversion probability needs a survey pair ("did an outreach worker tell you about the shelters?" × "did you already know?"). Then `lambdaOutreachPerDay = rate × conversion` drops straight into the existing channel (ContextCreator.java:275).

### 2.4 Identifiability without individual data

With only aggregate site-hour arrival counts A(t), the implied arrival intensity is roughly

```
a(t) ≈ N · h(t) · [p_aware(t) − F_departed(t)],   p_aware(t) = 1 − (1−p₀)(1−λ/24)^t
```

p₀ and the hazard scale α* are **confounded in level** (both scale early arrivals); λ is distinguished only through curvature (conversion grows the at-risk pool while departure depletes it — opposite-signed effects on a(t)). In practice: **fix p₀ by the informative Beta prior; then λ and α* become estimable from the arrival-timing shape, weakly.** This is precisely why the survey proportion is load-bearing: without it, aggregate data cannot separate "few knew" from "few chose to go" — the two stories the manuscript currently, correctly, refuses to distinguish (universal-awareness upper-bound hedge, audit inventory, md:289).

---

## 3. DESTINATION CHOICE: conditional logit over open shelters

### 3.1 Implemented utility (the drop-in target)

```
V_j = −betaTravelTime · walkTime_j(ownSpeed) + betaCapacityPrior · ln(max(1, cap_j))
```
over operating, open, network-reachable shelters not in the agent's `believedFull` set; deliberately **no live-occupancy filter** — fullness is discovered at the door and recorded as belief (GisAgent.java:682-717). Pet and adults-only policies act **at the door**, not in V_j (GisAgent.java:928-931, 944-951).

### 3.2 Estimation model

**McFadden conditional logit** on observed arrivals: chooser i (arriving at time t from origin o_i) faces the choice set S_it = {open, operating, reachable shelters}; chosen alternative = site of presentation. Alternative-specific covariates:

- **network walking time** — computable exactly with the existing Dijkstra route-tree infrastructure (the same `distanceTo`/`pathToSource` machinery, GisAgent.java:705, 732), so estimation and simulation share one distance definition;
- **ln capacity** (the engine's size prior);
- **pet-policy × pet-owner interaction** — *no engine slot in V_j*; if it loads, the drop-in route is the believedFull-style anticipatory channel or an engine extension, and the manuscript must say the estimated avoidance is not mechanically reproduced;
- **prior-refusal indicator** — maps to `believedFull` (monotone, never expires — GisAgent.java:459-467 field docs); identified **only from linked repeat attempts**, which requires person-identifiers across attempts in turnaway logs (currently ABSENT).

**Extensions:** nested logit with nests by facility type (congregate / motel / village — the 2026 inventory's `capacity_unit` column supports the nesting variable, audit inventory data section) to relax IIA; mixed logit with random `betaTravelTime` to capture taste heterogeneity (drop-in again requires the marginal-variance caveat of §1.3, since the engine's betas are scalars).

### 3.3 Power sketch — detectable-effect curves (standard formulas only)

For a conditional logit with a covariate standardized to unit within-choice-set SD, the per-arrival Fisher information is approximately `I₁ ≈ (1 − 1/J)` under roughly balanced shares; hence `SE(β̂) ≈ 1/√(N·I₁)` and the minimum detectable effect at two-sided α=0.05, power 0.80 is `MDE = 2.80·SE`. No effect size is assumed; the curves below are pure formula:

| N arrivals | MDE, J≥10 (I₁≈0.9) | MDE, J=2 (I₁=0.5) |
|---|---|---|
| 50 | 0.42 | 0.56 |
| 100 | 0.30 | 0.40 |
| 200 | 0.21 | 0.28 |
| 500 | 0.13 | 0.18 |
| 1000 | 0.094 | 0.125 |

(units: utility per within-set SD of the covariate; divide by the covariate's actual within-set SD to convert). Two consequences worth stating plainly. First, the **2020 event maxes out at N≈130 arrivals with J=2 open sites** (04-DECISION.md:70): MDE ≈ 2.80/√(130·0.5) ≈ **0.35 per SD** — only large effects are detectable, and with J=2 the model reduces to a binary logit on covariate differences, so `betaTravelTime` and `betaCapacityPrior` are estimable only if the two sites differ in both distance rank (person-specific — needs origin) and capacity (they did not: 99 vs 99, so **ln-capacity is a constant difference and betaCapacityPrior is unidentified from the 2020 event entirely**). Second, the present-day 36–48-site system (J large, capacity heterogeneous) is where choice estimation is actually powered — meaning the realistic instrument is **prospective arrival logging in the current system**, not archaeology on 2020.

---

## 4. ESTIMATION + CALIBRATION

### 4.1 Fitting

One joint Bayesian model (awareness HMM → hazard → choice, shared person attributes) in **Stan or PyMC** — the project's analysis layer is already Python (scripts/lint_claims.py, scripts/verify_2026_runs.py, scripts/verify_E_runs.py exist and run; audit inventory validation section), so PyMC integrates with the existing tooling with the least friction. NUTS; non-centered parameterization for θ; marginalized discrete awareness (§1.4). When only **aggregate** occupancy data exist, swap the individual likelihood for **simulation-based inference** (the engine itself is the simulator: fit by matching simulated site-hour occupancy curves at proposed parameter draws — ABC or neural SBI), which requires no new mechanism because the engine is already deterministic-given-seed and parameterized entirely through the batch surface (ContextCreator.java:274-294).

### 4.2 Prior-predictive checks (executable today)

Run the engine over prior draws; check that prior-predictive occupancy respects what is already known: (i) the one observed night ~90 + ~40 of 198 (04-DECISION.md:70) inside the prior-predictive band; (ii) implied attempt share consistent with the sourced pipeline 0.356 × 0.385 the current default was arithmetically tuned to (ContextCreator.java:279-282); (iii) the Wachinger constraint — high-barrier residents may never depart at peak PM2.5 (GisAgent.java:400-402) — retained as a sign restriction on κ (κ ≥ 0).

### 4.3 Held-out calibration (when data exist)

- **Temporal holdout:** fit on the first k nights of an event/season, score the remainder. (The repo's only within-repo temporal split candidate — the encampment `inc_date` column — splits inputs, not behavior; behavioral holdout requires new logs.)
- **Scores:** reliability diagrams by risk decile and **Brier** for person-level depart-by-horizon predictions; **CRPS** for nightly site occupancy counts; rank histograms / PIT for the SBI pathway.
- **Site holdout for choice:** leave-one-site-out predicted shares.

### 4.4 Posterior-predictive checks against site-hour occupancy

Simulate site-hour occupancy at posterior draws (M runs × existing seed protocol) and compare to logged occupancy. **Today this degenerates to a single-night interval check** against ~90/~40, and any wording must keep the claims-linter-enforced censored bracket (1.5–15.6×, with 1.52 never stated without 15.6 on the same line — audit inventory, claims.yaml:129-151) until a real occupancy series exists. Also run **simulation-based calibration** (SBC) on the fitted model — fully executable now with zero real data, and it validates the estimation code itself.

### 4.5 Guardrails carried over from the existing validation apparatus

Any engine change this framework motivates (area-correlated theta, distance-in-departure, anticipatory pet avoidance) goes behind the **R3 byte-identity null** (degenerate decision layer must reproduce archived arms byte-for-byte — audit inventory, scripts/verify_E_runs.py) and the registered-prediction discipline the project already practices (pre-registered directional predictions, misses kept as misses — audit inventory validation section). Fitted values replace registry rows only with evidence_class updated A → L and the sweep range replaced by the posterior interval.

---

## 5. FALLBACK: formal scenario-conditioned framing

If local estimation stays infeasible (the realistic near-term outcome — §Feasibility), the framework degrades gracefully into what the project already half-does, made formal:

1. **Priors become scenario axes.** Each ASSUMED coefficient keeps its registered sweep range (bRisk 0.25–0.55, wOfficial 0.6–1.7, γ 0–0.5, σθ 0.5–1.5, τ½ 12–72 h, κ 0.10–0.42, betaS ±1–2 orders — registry rows V35–V43, variables.csv:40-48, ranges per audit inventory) as its **declared axis**; results are reported as **bands over the axes**, never as point predictions; the two LOCAL behavioral quantities (0.356 awareness, 0.385 attempt-given-aware — ELayerSampler.java:46; ContextCreator.java:279-282) are the only anchored points and are named as such.
2. **Required manuscript wording** (verbatim candidates, consistent with the framing the linter already enforces — "improves outcomes under the modelled assumptions," never "recreates what happened," audit inventory, TECHNICAL_REFERENCE.md:2158-2170):
   - *"No coefficient in the departure or destination-choice layer is estimated from data on Multnomah County residents. All are declared scenario parameters with registered ranges; the awareness proportion (0.356) and attempt share (0.385), from one N=73 retrospective survey of this event, are the only event-specific behavioral quantities, and they enter as anchors, not estimates."*
   - *"Behavioral results are therefore scenario-conditioned: they state what follows under the declared decision model, not what the population did or would do."*
   - Every sentence quoting a behavioral outcome must carry the band over the declared axes or an explicit pointer to it.
3. **Enforcement:** add claims.yaml entries (the existing linter mechanism, scripts/lint_claims.py — executed green in the audit) that flag "estimated," "fitted," or "calibrated" adjacent to any V35–V43 coefficient name in deliverables. Design only — no file is modified by this task.

---

## 6. Estimable from OPERATIONAL data alone vs. requiring a SURVEY instrument

"Operational" = site-hour occupancy counts, timestamped arrival/turnaway logs with intake attributes (pet, dependents, coarse health, coarse origin). All are currently ABSENT from the repo (audit inventory: outreach logs ABSENT, communication timing ABSENT beyond one 211 sentence, turnaway logs ABSENT, no per-facility occupancy time series).

| Engine parameter (slot) | Operational data alone | Survey instrument needed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| α* = alphaHazard + wOfficial | **Yes** — arrival-timing curves, given N and an awareness prior | Denominator refinement | Only the sum is ever identifiable (GisAgent.java:414 open-gate collinearity) |
| wOfficial separately | **No** — structurally unidentifiable from arrivals | **Yes** — stated-intent items, or a cross-event announcement contrast | |
| bRisk, riskHalfLifeH | **Partially** — multi-day arrival timing against the PM series (shape identification) | — | Needs timestamps across ≥ several days; collinearity of all PM functionals (§1.2) limits precision |
| gammaVuln | Only if intake logs record COPD/asthma/age/mobility | Otherwise yes | Vulnerable flag defined at GisAgent.java:405-407 |
| sigmaTheta (θ variance) | **Weakly** — overdispersion of departure times (functional-form dependent) | **Yes** for credible identification — repeated-decision panel (nightly stay/return) or stated-choice replication | §1.3 frailty warning |
| σ_area (origin-area pooling) | Yes, if arrivals carry coarse origin | Origin question at intake | Disclosure floor: areas of ≥5 reports, never raw coordinates |
| κ_B, κ_P, κ_D (barrier costs) | **No** — arrivals condition on having departed; barriers act on non-departure | **Yes** — needs the non-attempter denominator (attributes of those who did not come) | The central selection problem: operational data never observes the people the barriers kept away |
| p₀ (pAwareInit) | **No** — confounded with α* in aggregate data (§2.4) | **Yes** — exists: 26/73 (ELayerSampler.java:43) | |
| lambdaOutreachPerDay | **Partially** — provider contact logs give the contact rate | Conversion-per-contact needs survey pair | λ = rate × conversion (§2.3) |
| betaTravelTime | Arrivals **with origin** (coarse) → yes | Otherwise yes (recalled origin) | Distance definition shared with engine Dijkstra (GisAgent.java:705) |
| betaCapacityPrior | **Yes**, in a multi-site system with capacity variation | — | Unidentified from the 2020 event (99 vs 99, §3.3) |
| Pet-policy avoidance in choice | Turnaway logs + linked repeat attempts | Stated avoidance | No V_j slot; engine handles pets at the door (GisAgent.java:941, 944-951) |
| Prior-refusal effect (believedFull) | Linked person-IDs across attempts | — | Privacy-heavy; likely infeasible operationally |
| Attempt-given-aware (0.385) | No | **Yes** — exists: 10/26 (04-DECISION.md, audit inventory V30) | Currently consumed only as the α calibration target (ContextCreator.java:279-282) |

**Instrument implications.** One modest **intake addendum** (5 items: pet, dependents, belongings, coarse origin area, "how did you hear about this shelter / when") attached to existing shelter intake would convert most "operational-partially" rows to "yes" for the *attempter* population. A **community survey** (the PSU instrument re-fielded prospectively, with a contact/awareness module) is irreducible for the denominators: p₀, λ conversion, and all κ. Nothing else can substitute, because refusal-to-depart is invisible to every operational system.

---

## Execution order (recommended)

1. **Now (no new data):** fallback formalization (§5) + prior library (§2.2, §4.2) + SBC/prior-predictive pipeline + power curves (§3.3) → this alone upgrades the manuscript's behavioral framing from implicit to formal.
2. **On agreement with a provider:** intake addendum + occupancy/arrival logging in the present-day system → §3 choice model and §1 hazard (α*, bRisk, τ½) become estimable within one smoke season.
3. **On survey funding:** re-fielded awareness/barrier survey → κ, p₀, λ close; registry rows flip A → L; sweeps collapse to posterior intervals.
data_requirements: Timestamped arrival logs at present-day shelters (person-level, hour resolution) with an anonymized person identifier linkable across attempts — currently ABSENT (no per-facility occupancy time series or arrival records exist in the repo; audit inventory data section)

Turnaway/refusal logs distinguishing capacity vs policy (pet, adults-only) refusals — ABSENT; the engine already separates these counters (recordPolicyRefusal per audit inventory, Shelter.java) so log schema should mirror them
Site-hour occupancy counts for at least one full smoke event or season — ABSENT; the only occupancy observation is one night, ~90+~40 of 198 (docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:70)

Intake addendum (5 items): pet ownership, accompanying dependents, heavy belongings, coarse origin area (>=5-report aggregation floor, never raw coordinates), and how/when the person learned of the shelter
Outreach provider contact logs (contacts per person-day) to identify the contact-rate half of lambdaOutreachPerDay — ABSENT and registered unsourced (A-31; variables.csv V41 row, per audit inventory)

Re-fielded community survey (PSU 'Stories from the Outside' instrument, prospective): awareness at onset, attempt-given-aware, barrier attributes of NON-attempters (the denominator operational data can never observe), outreach-contact/conversion pair (04-DECISION.md:44-63 documents the existing N=73 baseline)

Stated-intent items (would you have departed before official opening) or a cross-event announcement contrast — the only routes to identifying wOfficial separately from alphaHazard (structural collinearity at GisAgent.java:414)
Nightly stay/return decisions across shelter nights (linked) — the only credible identification for sigmaTheta (person frailty) beyond functional-form artifacts
Health attributes at intake (COPD/asthma/age band/mobility) if gammaVuln is to be estimated from operational data (vulnerable flag defined at GisAgent.java:405-407)

Primary-source confirmation of the 2020 99-per-site capacity and its unit (A-04, blocking) — any occupancy-based calibration is censored at a capacity whose unit is unconfirmed (audit inventory; assumptions.csv A-04)

IRB/consent and data-governance agreements consistent with the repo's disclosure posture (public remote already carries sensitive campsite data; k>=5 aggregation floors REPORTS not SITES — project memory note)
feasibility_now: Roughly one third of the framework runs today, and none of the estimation proper. Fully executable with repo-resident material: (1) the fallback formalization (section 5) — all sweep ranges already registered in variables.csv rows V35–V43 (lines 40-48) and the wording/linter machinery exists (scripts/lint_claims.py, executed green per the audit); (2) the prior library — Beta(26.5,47.5) awareness from 26/73 (ELayerSampler.java:43-46), attempt share 0.385 (ContextCreator.java:279-282), power-prior discount grid; (3) prior-predictive and SBC pipelines, since the engine is the simulator and every target coefficient is already a named batch parameter (ContextCreator.java:274-294) — no code change needed to run the engine at prior/posterior draws; (4) the power curves (section 3.3, formula-only). Executable as a single degenerate check: the posterior-predictive occupancy comparison, which today reduces to the one observed night (~90+~40 of 198, 04-DECISION.md:70) under the claims-linter-enforced 1.5–15.6x censored bracket. NOT executable now — zero rows of data exist for any likelihood term: no person-hour departure panel, no arrival timestamps, no turnaway logs, no outreach contact logs, no occupancy time series (all ABSENT per the audit inventory and 04-DECISION.md:82-89, which also records that no fitted choice model exists in any literature). Additionally, two coefficients are structurally unidentifiable from the 2020 event even if its records were recovered: wOfficial (open-gate collinearity, GisAgent.java:414) and betaCapacityPrior (both 2020 sites had capacity 99, so ln-capacity has zero within-set variance).
risks: Structural non-identifiability misread as estimation: wOfficial is perfectly collinear with alphaHazard in any engine-consistent data (departure requires open, GisAgent.java:414); reporting a 'fitted' wOfficial would be false precision — only the sum alpha* is estimable

Frailty (sigmaTheta) identification from single-spell data is functional-form-driven; a fitted variance could be an artifact of the logistic/z_R specification rather than real persistent heterogeneity

Selection problem is irreducible operationally: barrier coefficients (kappa) act by preventing arrivals, so arrival-conditioned data cannot identify them; skipping the survey and fitting kappa from operational data would produce biased-toward-zero estimates presented as local evidence

Drop-in mismatch: covariates that fit well but have no engine slot (PM dynamics, mobility main effect, pet avoidance in V_j, area-correlated theta) tempt silent engine divergence; every such finding must trigger either a registered engine extension behind the R3 byte-identity gate or explicit non-reproduction language

County-uniform PM2.5 makes all smoke covariates purely temporal and mutually collinear; bRisk/riskHalfLifeH estimates will be fragile to the z_R functional form and cannot be cross-validated spatially (2 in-county monitors; LOOCV declared unexecutable in SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT per audit inventory)

A-04 contamination: occupancy-based calibration is censored at a 99-per-site capacity whose unit (cots/positions/persons) is newsroom-sourced and unconfirmed (blocking assumption); fitted hazard scale absorbs this uncertainty

Nonstationarity: estimates from the present-day 36-48-site system transferred to 2020-style scenarios (and vice versa) assume behavioral stability across a system that changed size, composition, and policy — the same class of vintage mismatch the repo already documents for its inputs

Prior domination: with the realistic near-term data volume, posteriors on kappa, gammaVuln, sigmaTheta will substantially reflect priors; the manuscript must label them scenario-conditioned (section 5 wording) or the framework degrades into invented precision

Privacy/governance: linked arrival records and origin areas concern a highly vulnerable population, and the project's public remote already leaks sensitive location data (project memory: disclosure posture note); any logging design must clear the k>=5 report-aggregation floor and IRB before a single row is collected

Small-sample fragility of the 2020 record: N<=130 arrivals, J=2, capacity-constant choice sets — MDE ~0.35 SD for the hazard-relevant contrasts and betaCapacityPrior fully unidentified; retrofitting 2020 can validate direction only, never coefficients
